title: Forget Windows 12 for now, Microsoft wants Windows 11 to be rock-solid first
excerpt: Windows 11 still has plenty to fix first
content_html:
Published Nov 25, 2026, 2:32 PM EST

Anvinraj Valiyathara is a technology journalist with more than 15 years of experience covering the global tech industry. He has published over 20,000 articles across outlets including GizmoChina, Croma Unboxed, MySmartPrice, Pricebaba, Playfuldroid, BGR India, Free Press Journal, and IBTimes.

He specializes in tech news, leaks, smartphones, consumer electronics, and emerging technologies and has reviewed everything from phones and tablets to wearables.

Anvinraj is known for accuracy and for turning complex technical developments into clear, accessible stories. Outside work, he's a Formula 1 fan who loves to travel.

Microsoft is not committing to Windows 12 any time soon. Its top priority remains fixing Windows 11 while proving its AI features are actually worth using.

Windows chief Pavan Davuluri said in an interview with Axios that the company still has work to do on quality, craft, fundamentals, performance, and reliability across a Windows 11 base of more than one billion users. Only then does it earn permission to move on to what comes next.

That stance pushes back against rumors that Windows 12 was right around the corner, as frustration grows over buggy updates and pushy Copilot prompts. Earlier this year, Microsoft acknowledged its push to fix Windows 11’s core pain points with a public quality commitment. It promised fewer update interruptions, a faster File Explorer, and fewer unnecessary Copilot buttons in Notepad and Photos.

Microsoft isn't backing away from AI on the PC, though. Davuluri says the company must build the underlying tech for future AI apps and prove people find those tools useful, especially developers, creators, and knowledge workers. At Ignite, Microsoft previewed local file actions and read-only PC diagnostics for Copilot+, plus hybrid routing between on-device models and the cloud.

Hardware limits are also slowing down the next Window shift

Rising memory costs and uneven AI traction keep Windows 11 in place

On-device AI still demands far more hardware than most everyday laptops carry. Davuluri expects models with 10 billion to 20 billion parameters to bring richer local AI to PCs.

That runs straight into the worsening global RAM shortage, with analyst Bobo O’Donnell noting heavier models pushing buyers toward 32GB, 64GB, or 128GB machines. Meanwhile, Microsoft had to tune memory compression and background tasks just to keep 8GB Windows 11 PCs responsive.

On-device AI still demands far more hardware than most everyday laptops carry

A quick jump past Windows 11 would also disrupt businesses, many of which only recently finished moving off Windows 10. Plenty of everyday users still see built-in AI as overhead, and some have resorted to disabling Copilot on Windows 11 altogether. Davuluri also didn’t rule out Windows 12 or share a release schedule. Until Windows 11 feels rock-solid and its AI feels genuinely useful, Microsoft is sticking with the operating system people already have.
